findings.title: The run/condition directory ({arm?} layout facet) is not an AER field, so 675 of 990 executions share their task identity with executions of other dirs
findings.check: L2 identity (prereg section 6; prereg section 3 'Run' row already anticipated the arm comes only from the path)
findings.evidence: In the 90 sampled executions the arm string occurs only at /artifacts/*/origin/path (80/80 e2e executions; the 10 base executions have no e2e component) and in 80/90 PROV documents through that path; 0/90 SEM files. ext.agentdojo keys error/pipeline_name/task_kind only; task.attack_id carries no run index; no arm string in execution source_key/unit/src/id/ex. Population: e2e_tap_* and e2e_seeded_pair_* labels cover 63 logs each = 3 runs x 21, so 630 attacked executions are in 3-way identity collisions; the 45 pre-pass executions (attack_id null, task_id injection_task_k) collide 9-way across all dirs; total 675/990. Sample tuples: 45 singletons + 5 groups of 9. Phase10d routing R5 pattern (ceferisbarov, proposed agentdojo.attack_arm_from_path@1), which does not name this profile. No outcome bias: per-dir rates from the origin path give AER = raw on 90/90.
findings.hypothesis_ref: prereg section 3 (Run row), section 6 L2 identity
findings.recommendation: Widen R5 (class-I rule agentdojo.attack_arm_from_path@1 writing the {arm?} facet to ext.agentdojo.attack_arm) to this profile before the round, covering the pre-pass executions too. Until then key per-arm statistics on the origin path and disclose that the attack label does not identify the run.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran armptr.py; checked other AER execution fields (none carries the arm); prereg section 3 already anticipates the facet is path-only, so the expectation is met through the origin path and the class is expected-known under R2 (R5 routing). Corrected severity S2 -> S3 (R5 entry sets none; no outcome bias) and the count 630 -> 675 (45 pre-pass executions collide 9-way).

findings.title: C0/DEL code points in 53 model-written tool-call channel arguments (41 logs, e2e candidate conditions only); every such call fails
findings.check: L1-03 encodings (classify), plus how L2 serialises the same strings
findings.evidence: L1-03: c0 in 41/990 artefacts (129 strings), cr 2, fffd 1, at args/channel 53 and error 23. 53 calls in 41 logs, arg key 'channel' 53/53, all 53 ValueError 'channel does not exist'. By dir: persona_v3 8, seeded_pair 8, seeded_pair_run1 5, seeded_pair_run2 5, tap 4, tap_run1 6, tap_run2 5; base 0, baseline 0. 0 of 51 candidate files and 0 tool outputs contain a C0 character; raw bytes hold them as JSON \u00XX escapes (plus a few \b, \f). Mechanism: the model copies the long injected channel name (channel arg up to 2,069 chars) garbled, with control characters in place of some characters; the C0 is one part of the mismatch, not shown to be the sole cause of the failure. Model output recorded faithfully; no control-char handling in upstream code. The 3 sampled logs keep the escapes in AER 3/3 and PROV 3/3 (j1 and j2) and validate.
findings.reproduction: uv run python ~/.agentprov/migration-work/precheck/hilarytorn-trajectory-poisoning/exam/h8c0.py ~/.agentprov/staging/10c/hilarytorn/in-context-trajectory-poisoning.git d71ab8bc2aa9db35ff443cc81e475e70ee8da215 <out> -> c0_logs_by_arm baseline 0, <none> 0, e2e arms 8/8/5/5/4/6/5; all 53 c0 calls errored; cand files_with_c0 0; c0labels.py -> 41 labels, 3 in sample
findings.recommendation: Disclose in the datasheet. Non-JSON PROV serialisations and transcript renderers must escape C0. Route the proposed artefacts.toml entry to the family owner; no mapping change.
findings.artefact_proposal: [[artefact]] id = "agentdojo.art.control_chars_in_model_args"; title = "Control characters in model-written tool arguments"; description = "The model copies a long injected string (slack: a channel name holding the injection) into a tool argument, garbled, with C0/DEL code points in place of some characters; the call fails with a tool error (channel does not exist); AER and PROV keep the code points as JSON escapes"; scope = {sources=["hilarytorn-trajectory-poisoning"], parts=["head"], profiles=["hilarytorn-trajectory-poisoning"]}; cause = "model output (gpt-4o-2024-05-13) on spliced monitor-priming candidates, not the harness"; detector = "L1-03 c0 class at /messages/*/tool_calls/*/args/*"; claims = ["tool-error rates of the e2e conditions include these failed calls"]; recorded_as = "verbatim args in AER and PROV apv:args; tool_execution status error"; handling = "disclose; escape on non-JSON serialisation"; expected = [{snapshot="head", count=41, unit="logs (53 calls, all errored)", basis="precheck L1-03 + exam", status="verified"}]; refs = ["docs/reports/precheck/data/hilarytorn-trajectory-poisoning/os-population.json"]

verdicts.reasoning: Independent recount through l1_scan readers and agentprov.ingest: 41 logs, 53 calls, 'channel' 53/53; ruled out environment-carried C0 (0 in tool outputs), harness mangling (no upstream handling) and tool invention (escapes present in raw blobs). No artefacts.toml entry covers it: R1 source-defect, S3. Wording correction: each call fails because the channel name is mismatched/garbled; C0 is one part of it.

findings.title: The prereg expected about 270 sampled units (25 attacked per arm); the pre-registered rule with the hook's stratum key gives 90 (5 per arm)
findings.check: L2 sample design vs prereg section 4 (README amendment 2.4); rule R4
findings.evidence: The family hook's stratum key is arm x attack_family (18 strata: 9 attacked of 105 + 9 pre-pass of 5; 5 each = 90), not the (dir, attack label) key the prereg assumed (its 'attack label' meant the injection task, which is not part of the hook key). Every attacked arm has n = 5 < 20, so the sample gap rule applies to no arm; outcome sanity rests on the exact population check (H1, H2). With one attacked stratum per arm the post-stratified rate equals the plain rate.
findings.recommendation: Record in the dossier (R4, prereg author). The post-check reuses the 90-label list unchanged; the prereg is not edited.

verdicts.reasoning: Sample file: n=90, 18 strata, quota 5 each. The tool applies the pre-registered rule as written (amendment 2.4: hook key, no data-dependent re-keying), so the prereg expectation is what is wrong: R4 documentation-mismatch S3. H1/H2 hold on the population, so no outcome coverage is lost.

findings.title: l2_check keys outcomes on model|defence|attack, pooling the three runs of tap and of seeded_pair; the arm facet is aliased to defence in the facet table
